result_summary: Final Riksdag seats: Social Democrats 99, Moderates 70, Sweden Democrats 62, Left 30, Centre 25, Christian Democrats 22, Greens 22 and Liberals 19. S+C+V+MP total 176 of 349 seats.
government_summary: Ulf Kristersson leads a caretaker government from 17 September. Magdalena Andersson resumed exploratory formation talks on 5 October, with a report due to the Speaker by 12 October; a successor taking office has not been verified.

sources.title: Government of Sweden: Kristersson caretaker-government notice
Riksdag: Andersson formation mandate resumes, 2 October 2026

coverage_note: The incumbent movement represents caretaker continuity only. Election results and formation talks do not establish a successor policy bundle.

result_summary: The Central Election Commission provisional allocation gives United List 41 seats, Latvia First 17, Sovereign Power/Young Latvians 15, National Alliance 10, Progressives 10 and New Unity 7, out of 100.
government_summary: Andris Kulbergs has led the Cabinet since 28 May 2026, replacing Evika Siliņa before the election. The President announced on 6 October that Kulbergs and United List would begin forming a post-election government; its appointment has not been verified.

sources.title: Central Election Commission: provisional 15th Saeima results
Cabinet of Ministers: Kulbergs government assumes office
President of Latvia: statement on formation, 6 October 2026

coverage_note: The start date records the pre-election Kulbergs Cabinet, not a completed post-election formation. Successor movement and axes remain uncoded pending enacted-policy evidence.

result_summary: The official result certified on 7 November 2025 awarded D66 and PVV 26 seats each, VVD 22, GroenLinks-PvdA 20 and CDA 18 in the 150-seat House.
government_summary: Rob Jetten's D66-VVD-CDA Cabinet was sworn in on 23 February 2026, replacing the Schoof government.

sources.title: Government of the Netherlands: Jetten government sworn in

coverage_note: Government formation is verified. A Jetten policy-content movement and axis assessment remain pending enacted-policy review.

result_summary: The final national allocation gave Freedom Movement 29 seats, SDS 28, NSi-SLS-Fokus 9, Social Democrats 6, Democrats 6, Left-Vesna 5 and Resni.ca 5, plus the two national-minority seats.
government_summary: The National Assembly appointed Slovenia's 16th government, led by Janez Janša, on 4 June 2026, replacing Robert Golob's government.

sources.title: State Election Commission: final National Assembly result in official gazette
Government of Slovenia: members and appointment of the 16th government

result_summary: The final mainland allocation gave Social Democrats 38 seats, SF 20, Venstre 18, Liberal Alliance and Danish People's Party 16 each, Moderates 14, Conservatives 13, Red-Green Alliance 11, Radikale and Denmark Democrats 10 each, Alternative 5 and Citizens' Party 4. The 175 mainland seats exclude two each from Greenland and the Faroe Islands.
government_summary: Mette Frederiksen's third Cabinet took office on 3 June 2026, comprising Social Democrats, SF, Moderates and Radikale Venstre. This replaced the previous Social Democrats-Venstre-Moderates coalition.

result_summary: The 34th Dáil election returned Fianna Fáil 48 seats, Sinn Féin 39 and Fine Gael 38 of 174 seats.
government_summary: Micheál Martin was appointed Taoiseach on 23 January 2025 and announced the new government; Simon Harris became Tánaiste. The Harris-led government is no longer current.

result_summary: The 2025-2029 Storting has Labour 53, Progress 47, Conservatives 24, Socialist Left 9, Centre 9, Red 9, Greens 8, Christian Democrats 7 and Liberals 3 seats.
government_summary: Jonas Gahr Støre continues to lead an all-Labour minority Cabinet. The 16 September 2025 post-election ministerial changes retained Støre as prime minister and Jens Stoltenberg as finance minister.

sources.title: Office of the Prime Minister: Cabinet changes, 16 September 2025

coverage_note: Labour continuity is verified; external parliamentary support does not make other parties Cabinet members. Existing policy-axis coding is retained without treating the result as new enactment evidence.
